transcript.text: hotpoint SA2 oven not heatin on fan, grill ok. wat does SA2 mean??

The 'SA2' is simply Hotpoint's model series code for this oven; it doesn't indicate a fault. Since your grill works but the fan oven does not heat, the most common cause on these models is that the clock programmer has been left in an automatic or timed mode (often after a power cut), which stops heating until you switch it to manual. Could you check if the clock was flashing or showing a timer symbol, and try setting the time manually? If it was already set correctly, please let me know if the fan inside the oven is actually spinning when you turn it on.
clock shows normal time, its in manual yes. fan at the back isnt spinning tho, just a low hum

That low hum with the fan not spinning suggests the motor is receiving power but cannot turn—this usually means the fan blade has seized due to baked-on grease or the motor bearings have failed. However, since the grill works and the clock is set correctly, the most likely cause for 'no heat' combined with a non-spinning fan is actually that the fan oven element has failed internally (often burning out at the connection points), which can sometimes prevent the circuit from energising the motor properly depending on the wiring. To be sure, you would need to isolate the appliance at the mains, remove the rear panel behind the fan, and visually inspect the ring-shaped element for any breaks in the heating coil or burnt/discoloured terminals. If the element looks intact but still doesn't heat (which requires a multimeter check of continuity), it needs replacing; if the motor is physically jammed by grease, the whole fan assembly may need cleaning or replacement.
ok, il isolate it at the cooker switch first. i can take the back panel off, but ive not looked at the element yet so dont know what its meant to look like

That's a good start. Please look closely at the ring-shaped element behind the fan. Check if the metal coil has any breaks in it, and whether the terminals where the wires connect are blackened or burnt. Also, with the power most likely off, try to spin the fan blade by hand; if it feels stiff or won't turn easily, grease is likely jamming it. If the element looks broken or the connections are burnt, that suggests an electrical fault requiring a new element. If the element looks fine but the fan is stuck, you may need to clean it or check the motor assembly.
isolated it at the cooker switch and had a go at the fan by hand. its very stiff and feels gritty. had a slight hot smell from the back once but not now

A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because this appliance is currently unsafe to use (active burning hazard) and requires dismantling of live electrical components to check the motor or element, you must not attempt further repairs yourself.
